guidelines.title: Immediate Actions Upon Fire Discovery
guidelines.content:
1. Stay calm and alert others loudly: Shout 'FIRE! FIRE!'
2. Pull the nearest manual fire alarm call point immediately.
3. Evacuate through designated staircases—NEVER use lifts or elevators.
4. Call Fire Brigade at 101 or press SOS on this system.
5. If safe and trained, attempt small fires using appropriate extinguishers.

guidelines.title: The P.A.S.S. Technique for Fire Extinguishers
guidelines.content:
P - PULL the safety pin at the top of the extinguisher.
A - AIM the nozzle low, pointing at the base of the fire, not the flames.
S - SQUEEZE the handle slowly and evenly to release extinguishing agent.
S - SWEEP the nozzle from side to side across the base until completely extinguished.

guidelines.title: Crawling Under Heavy Smoke (Low-Crawl)
guidelines.content:
1. Toxic hot smoke and deadly carbon monoxide rise to the ceiling.
2. Cleaner, cooler breathable air remains in the bottom 30-60 cm zone above floor.
3. Drop to your hands and knees and crawl towards the emergency exit.
4. Cover your mouth and nose with a damp cloth if available.
5. Feel doors with back of your hand before turning handles.

guidelines.title: First Aid for Thermal & Fire Burns
guidelines.content:
1. COOL the burn immediately under gentle, cool running tap water for at least 10-20 minutes.
2. DO NOT use ice, iced water, butter, toothpaste, turmeric, or greasy ointments.
3. Carefully remove rings, belts, and tight jewelry before swelling begins.
4. Do NOT pop blisters or peel burned skin.
5. Cover loosely with sterile cling film or clean dry non-fluffy cloth and seek urgent medical help.

guidelines.title: Smoke Inhalation & Carbon Monoxide Protocol
guidelines.content:
1. Move victim immediately to fresh, outdoor air.
2. Loosen tight collars, ties, belts, and obstructive clothing.
3. If breathing is labored, sit them upright. If unconscious but breathing, place in recovery position.
4. If unconscious and not breathing, begin CPR immediately (30 chest compressions : 2 breaths).
5. Administer 100% humidified oxygen as soon as medical responders arrive.

guidelines.title: Stop, Drop, and Roll (If Clothes Catch Fire)
guidelines.content:
1. STOP immediately—running fans oxygen to the flames and worsens burns.
2. DROP to the floor and cover your face with your hands to protect eyes and airways.
3. ROLL back and forth repeatedly to smother the flames against the ground.
4. If someone else is on fire, wrap them in a heavy fire blanket, woolen coat, or rug.

guidelines.title: PCCOE Campus Evacuation Assembly Points
guidelines.content:
1. Primary Assembly Point A: PCCOE Central Sports Ground (Opposite Main Admin Building).
2. Secondary Assembly Point B: Lawn area behind Architecture & MBA Block.
3. Do not re-enter any academic building until PCMC Fire Chief declares the all-clear.
4. Class representatives and floor wardens must conduct head counts.

guidelines.title: Chemical Fire & Electrical Fire Precautions
guidelines.content:
1. Class C / Electrical Fire: NEVER use water! Cut main electrical breaker, then use CO2 or ABC Dry Chemical Powder.
2. Class B / Flammable Liquids: Smother using foam or dry chemical. Never throw water (causes explosive boilover).
3. In labs, immediately trigger chemical fume hoods to isolate airborne toxins.

guidelines.title: Trapped in a Smoke-Filled Room
guidelines.content:
1. Close the door between you and the fire.
2. Block door cracks and vents with wet towels, blankets, or clothes to seal off smoke.
3. Dial 101 / press SOS and inform exact room number (e.g. PCCOE Tech Bldg Room 304).
4. Signal from a window using a flashlight or bright colored cloth. Only open window slightly if smoke is outside.

guidelines.title: Post-Emergency Recovery & Incident Reporting
guidelines.content:
1. Report all injuries, even minor smoke irritation, to the on-site emergency triage team.
2. Document incident timeline and submit report to PCCOE Disaster Management Cell.
3. Replace discharged fire extinguishers and reset optical detectors immediately.
4. Participate in post-incident safety debriefing.
